findings.title: Function/class edge endpoints contradict the slice's own read discipline
findings.description: The design requires, in Section 6 detail, that "Function- and class-level edge endpoints are resolved to their owning file's layer rather than dropped, so a `calls` edge between two functions in different layers still counts as an inter-layer signal." This is in direct tension with three statements of the read discipline: the architecture ("function- and class-level nodes are not read"), this slice's own "Read discipline, unchanged" section (line ~330, "the excluded 687 function and class nodes remain excluded"), and Success Criterion 9 ("no function- or class-level node is read"; walkthrough step 7: "no function- or class-level node data appears in any section"). Resolving an edge endpoint to a function's owning file requires consuming function/class node identity, which is excluded by the discipline the design claims to leave unchanged. The design never reconciles these. State explicitly whether this is derived purely from parsing edge-ID strings (not node reads) and whether such counts may appear in a section, or drop the clause — otherwise implementers get contradictory instructions on a boundary the architecture treats as a principle.

findings.title: "Corrections to the 361 contract" assume 361 skill text that is neither specified nor present yet
findings.description: The design's stated reason for being ("the reason this slice is not merely additive") is two corrections premised on specific defects in 361's *generated skill*: "The 361 skill states that `nodeIds` mixes file, function, and class nodes and instructs intersecting with `type == "file"`" (line 121) and "361's skill text collapsed that to `select(.type == "file")`" (line 146). Neither claim matches the 361 slice design, which says only "each layer's name, description, and file count, from `layers[]`" and uses `select(.type == "file" or ...)` (an allow-list, not a bare `== "file"`). Moreover 361 is `not_started` and `commands/analysis/understand.md` does not currently exist (`commands/analysis/` holds only `tech-debt-audit.md`). The consumer's expectations of its prerequisite therefore don't match the prerequisite as designed. The underlying end-state (count layers as `nodeIds|length`; exclude `function`/`class` by name) is architecturally correct and should be kept, but it should be stated unconditionally as part of the extraction mapping, or made explicitly conditional on observing that text at implementation time — not asserted as fact about an artifact that doesn't exist and whose design says otherwise.

findings.title: Design is overweight relative to the slice's assigned scope; name what to cut
findings.description: The slice plan assigns 362: the field-to-section extraction mapping (fields/order/fallback), the unchanged read discipline, and the `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` reuse decision (effort 3/5, risk Low). The design carries materially more: a large empirical "Verified graph facts" table; an extensive "Corrections to the 361 contract" apparatus with type-breakdown tables, cross-checks, and a dedicated risk mitigation; and a new seven-section "Coverage and scope limits" section that closes three 361 deferrals (`config.json` key reporting, `.understandignore` listing, `analyzedFiles` discrepancy detection). The architecture's comprehension output lists only layers, complexity hotspots, entry points, and dependency observations, and neither 363 nor 364 consumes the coverage section. Cuttable/deferrable: (a) trim the "Verified graph facts" table to the few numbers the decisions actually depend on — it is re-measured in walkthrough step 1 anyway; (b) defer the coverage/scope-limits section and its discrepancy handling to a later slice, since it is not assigned here and feeds no downstream slice; (c) once Finding 2 is resolved by stating the correct end-state, the correction-specific measurement tables and cross-check machinery shrink substantially.
